doc.title: Ralph LaLama interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, May 23, 2010

title: Naming Sonny Rollins and Hank Mobley as influences
summary: Asked whom he sounds like, LaLama picks Rollins and Mobley; Rowe liked the Mobley tune opening the concert.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: I wanted to pose a question to you. If you were able to write your own entry about yourself for a new coming jazz book, like a jazz encyclopedia, and you could actually write it yourself, you might say, “ Ralph LaLama sounds reminiscent of” blank and blank. Like two tenor players.
I would probably have to say Sonny Rollins and Hank Mobley.
Well you know it’s interesting because the guy who wrote the entry for the Grove Encyclopedia of Jazz said exactly that.

Yeah. I’m not sure of his name but I just looked in there and that’s exactly what it said, that those were like big influences on you. And I noticed yesterday, I was so pleased when you started out the concert with that Hank Mobley tune.
Oh yeah, “Dis I Dig of You” that’s right.
Not many people — well at least in my experience — have heard that played a lot.
